students.preparation: Bachelor’s degree + MD or DO + family medicine residency

steps.title: Explore a health question
steps.detail: Use two reliable sources to explain a general health question. Notice whether you enjoy the science, explanation, or both. Use a public youth program for supervised exposure to healthcare.

steps.title: Map college, medical school, and residency
steps.detail: Compare college prerequisites, four-year medical training, and family medicine residency. Budget each stage separately; no college major guarantees medical school admission.

steps.title: Ask about a normal day in family medicine
steps.detail: Ask a physician and a resident about patient contact, documentation, training hours, and what they wish they knew in high school.

steps.title: Build three pieces for a small portfolio
steps.detail: Design a poster, a simple visual identity, and a digital layout. Ask for feedback and revise one piece. Notice whether critique and revisions hold your interest.

steps.title: Compare affordable design programs
steps.detail: Compare curriculum, portfolio review, internships, software access, net price, and transfer credit. College can build skills and connections; employment still depends on demonstrated work.

steps.title: Ask an employed designer about early-career work
steps.detail: Ask about deadlines, client feedback, portfolio expectations, and full-time roles versus freelance hours and business expenses.

steps.title: Explore electrical work safely
steps.detail: Visit a public training demonstration or approved student program. Practice algebra, measurement, and reading diagrams. Do not work on live wiring.

steps.title: Compare a paid apprenticeship and college options
steps.detail: Austin ETA combines four years and 8,000 hours of training. Review admission steps, published pay, tuition, tools, and Texas licensing. Affordable technical or business college study can add options.

steps.title: Ask an apprentice and a qualified electrician
steps.detail: Ask about hours, travel to job sites, physical demands, tuition, and how pay changes with completed training. Distinguish an employer schedule from the regional wage proxy.
